issue_context.title: Add PodPriority to preemption_victims metrics in scheduler
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

I propose enhancing the scheduler's preemption_victims metrics by including PodPriority information. This addition will provide more detailed insights into the preemption process, helping to understand which pods are being preempted and why, based on their priority.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d61cbac69aae97db1839bd2e0e86d68f26b353a7/pkg/scheduler/metrics/metrics.go#L86-L94

### Why is this needed?

Including PodPriority in the preemption_victims metrics is essential for providing a more complete view of the scheduler's decision-making process. Currently, the metrics provide the count of preempted pods but lack detailed information about their priority. With this enhancement, administrators and developers can better analyze preemption patterns and priorities, leading to more informed decisions and potentially improving cluster efficiency and scheduling fairness.

review_comments: This is a STABLE metric, I think this is not acceptable, right? @logicalhan
Oh, sorry, I didn't know that. Is there relevant documentation? Can't I just add a tag? I believe this change doesn't introduce breaking changes for users.

I believe @kerthcet is correct.  From https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/metrics/#list-of-stable-kubernetes-metrics:

> Stable metrics observe strict API contracts and no labels can be added or removed from stable metrics during their lifetime.
I completely didn't know that either, good to know.
Thanks for your guide 🙏 Is adding the new metrics the only way to achieve https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122046?

Yes, and I'm honestly not sure this feature request deserves creating a new metric.
@kerthcet What do you think.
Yes, keeping two similar metrics is not a good idea. Maybe we can back to this once we got similar feedbacks from the community.
I don't think it is worth creating new metrics for this feature( but I think it's valuable labels). Should I close this PR
